question.text: A big drop is formed by coalescing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn></math> small identical drops of water. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> be the total surface energy of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn></math> small drops of water and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> be the surface energy of single big drop of water, the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mn>1</mn></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></math>________.

solution.text:
Let radius of the small drop be r and the radius of the big drop be R. Then, total volume will remain constant, therefore

1000×ρ43πr3=43πR3ρ

⇒R=10r

Initial total surface energy, E1=1000×4πr2×S and 

E2=4π(10r)2 S

⇒E1E2=101Hence, x=10.
